perspective:
Ethan’s available information:

- He is Ethan Mohamud, a Black man and plumber; he knows his own background and occupation.
- Gary Guo is his long-time close friend; they met in middle school. Ethan knows Gary is a man, Asian, and a doctor.
- Ethan noticed Gary working excessively long hours at the hospital, often skipping meals and sacrificing sleep. This worried him.
- Ethan invited Gary to a two-day weekend retreat, saying Gary’s health mattered and it might give him a new perspective.
- Ethan heard Gary decline, saying he appreciated the concern but couldn’t go because there was too much to do at the hospital.
- During the retreat, Ethan observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. Ethan suspected there was more than just professional obligation.
- Ethan confronted Gary, saying they had been friends since middle school and Gary could tell him anything without judgment.
- Ethan heard Gary say it was complicated and that he didn’t want to burden Ethan.
- Gary opened up to Ethan about pressures managing a new department and personal challenges he was facing.
- Ethan felt relief and empathy, then suggested prioritizing tasks and delegating some responsibilities.
- Ethan heard Gary agree, saying he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in with Gary and discussed his progress and remaining challenges.
- Ethan heard Gary say things were better, he was less overwhelmed thanks to Ethan’s help, and he had time for a movie the previous weekend. Ethan felt hopeful and proud.
- After a year, Ethan observed Gary had adjusted to a healthier work-life balance and could manage on his own. Ethan felt satisfied and happy for him.
- Ethan decided to step back but told Gary he was always just a call away. Ethan heard Gary thank him and say he felt more in control now.
